item.title: In new novel, multiple voices tell the story of 'Good People'
item.description: The book centers around an Afghan refugee family who are an American success at first, until a family tragedy causes them to become a national scandal.

item.title: Winter got you down? Here's how to beat the winter blues
item.description: Disruptive winter storms from the Midwest to the Northeast and cold fronts in the South may have you feeling out of sorts.

item.title: Trump's dare to Democrats was one of the big moments in his SOTU speech
item.description: President Trump dared Democrats to stand and swear an oath "to protect American citizens, not illegal aliens."

item.title: Joachim Trier on directing choices in Oscar-nominated 'Sentimental Value'
item.description: The Norwegian film "Sentimental Value" is up for nine Oscars, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Original Screenplay.

item.title: The story of America's biggest and best homegrown diamonds
item.description: The United States does not have a rich diamond mining history. But an exhibit at the Smithsonian Institute proves that some of the world’s most dazzling gems are homegrown.

item.title: How social pressures affect young clownfish
item.description: In some clownfish, those famous stripes disappear as they grow up.

item.title: Harvard professor Larry Summers resigning after Epstein revelations
item.description: Larry Summers, the former Harvard University president whose personal relationship to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein caused him to step back from teaching duties last fall, will retire from his university professorship and all other faculty appointments at the end of the year, a university spokesperson said.

item.title: Trump administration's 'third country' deportation policy is unlawful, Mass. federal judge rules
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in the administration’s favor last year, pausing the judge's previous decision and clearing the way for a flight carrying several migrants to complete its trip to war-torn South Sudan, where they had no ties.

item.title: Celebrating Ramadan while living in fear
item.description: Muslims around the world are celebrating the holy month of Ramadan. But for immigrant communities in the U.S., those celebrations are being tempered by fears of ICE.

item.title: Giving warmth and a charge on Cape Cod after the big storm
item.description: Eastham Public Library has been able to serve as a warming and charging center for area residents because it has a generator. And businesses including Atlantic Spice Shop in Truro are gradually re-opening and providing a little warmth and sustenance to residents, as well.
